editorial:
You follow Roger Ferris, a CIA agent working on the ground in the Middle East, as he hunts a dangerous terrorist leader. Back in the United States, his boss Ed Hoffman watches everything through satellite feeds and makes big calls from a safe distance. The tension between these two men drives the whole story. Ferris has to build trust with local allies, especially a Jordanian intelligence chief named Hani, while Hoffman keeps pulling strings behind his back. The movie feels gritty and real, with dusty streets, crowded markets, and sudden bursts of violence. You never quite know who is telling the truth, keeping you on edge.

Leonardo DiCaprio and Russell Crowe both deliver strong performances, and their clashing styles make every scene crackle. The action is sharp and well-staged, and the pacing rarely slows down. On the downside, the plot can feel a bit complicated, and some side characters do not get enough screen time. Still, if you enjoy smart spy thrillers with real stakes, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ferris is captured and tortured by the terrorist group after Hoffman's plan goes wrong. Hani rescues him but is furious about being used. Ferris recovers in a hospital, where Hoffman visits and tries to smooth things over. Realizing he can no longer trust the agency, Ferris quits the CIA. He then travels to see Aisha, the nurse he fell in love with, hoping to start a quieter life away from the spy world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart spy thrillers with real stakes.
